_comment: Single source of truth for QA rules for the top_community_issues experiment. Edit here only — qa_validate.py reads this at runtime; no Python changes needed. Encodes the issue-evaluation rubric (verified/unverified/incorrect via claim-level supported/unsupported/contradicted) onto the QA spine. Run: `uv run python qa_validate.py path/to/top_community_issues.json --product-spec top_community_issues_product_spec.json`.
_output_format_comment: structured_json: the artifact is one JSON object. Layer-1 jsonschema validation runs against the experiment manifest's output_schema before any claim check. This product cites provenance via claims[]/sources[], not inline prose citations, so citation_paths is empty and the inline checks self-skip.
_priority_filter_comment: This product emits issues[] (not the spine's optional items[]), so no top-level items match this filter and the items-based checks (priority_count_nonzero, claim_coverage) stay inert by design. priority_required_status is intentionally unset so priority_count_nonzero never blocks. Kept for config completeness.
_claim_types_comment: The high-weight/blockable types are the load-bearing facts from the rubric (a contradiction on any of them makes the issue Incorrect -> block). Medium types cap at Unverified (warn) when unsupported. Low types (lean annotation, synthesis) never block. A claim_type absent from source_hierarchy yields a non-blocking diagnostic surfacing the policy gap.
_accuracy_categories_comment: Judge verdict grouping. ok = the rubric's Supported (verbatim/consistent) plus reasonable inference and labeled-modeled leans. not_ok = the rubric's Unsupported (Not in Source / Unverifiable) and Contradicted (Incorrect). A not_ok high-weight/blockable claim blocks the release (issue was Incorrect); a not_ok lower-weight claim warns (issue capped at Unverified). 'Not in Source — Verified Elsewhere' stays not_ok: if corroboration exists it should have been flattened into sources[], where the judge would classify it Accurate/Directionally Consistent instead.
_prohibited_phrases_comment: top_community_issues summaries are descriptive, not imperative EO-advice prose, so no imperative-verb blocklist applies. Empty -> the prohibited_phrases check self-skips.
_citation_paths_comment: No inline [Label](URL) citations in this artifact — provenance lives in claims[]/sources[]. Empty -> the inline citation-coherence, social-media-citation, and inline-URL checks self-skip.
_url_check_comment: HTTP liveness for cited source URLs — the rubric's step-1 URL head-check. Advisory (dead/unreachable URLs annotate, never block), SSRF-hardened. Probes the top-level sources[].url.
_coherence_check_comment: Per-priority-item summary-vs-source coherence is a meeting_briefing (items[].display.summary) mechanism and is diagnostic-only regardless. This product carries no items[], so disable to keep the bundle clean; claim-level triage is the accuracy instrument here.
_structured_validators_comment: Labels the numeric_review_flag for the judge (detection-only; never blocks). Maps the numeric high-weight claim_types to a literal kind so the judge is handed the figures to confirm. kind is one of: money, date, vote_count, legal_citation, percentage, name.
_source_hierarchy_comment: claim_type -> allowed source_types (manifest source enum: news, government_website, research, poll, advocacy_org). A high-weight fact may not rest solely on an advocacy_org or poll: figures/dates/votes must come from news/government/research. Resident-demand attribution is the inverse — it must come from resident-voice sources (op-ed news, advocacy orgs, a resident survey poll, or 311 on a government site). A violating high-weight claim blocks; others annotate. Types with no entry (background_context, lean_annotation, synthesis) get a non-blocking diagnostic.
_embedding_rescue_blocklist_comment: Numbers, dates, votes, and named-existence claims must never be rescued by semantic similarity ($1.8M vs $2M embeds ~0.99). Coherence rescue is disabled product-wide anyway; kept for correctness if it is ever re-enabled.
_judges_comment: Phase 1 triage + Phase 2 adversarial escalation. Names resolve via the QA_JUDGES env var (name:provider:model,...). Same-family Anthropic (Sonnet Phase 1 + Opus Phase 2) is the in-Fargate path. This IS the Claude adjudication the rubric was built around.
_completeness_comment: Annotate-only substance floors (never blocks). Measures the issues[] prose since this product has no executive_summary/items[]. min_priority_items is omitted (no items[] to count). Floors are deliberately low: a tight 1-to-3-issue lead is the correct product, not a defect.
_coverage_check_comment: Per-item claim coverage joins on items[].id, which this product does not emit. Disabled — under-decomposition is instead guarded by the spot-check in instruction.md and by high_weight_claims_have_extracts.
_polish_comment: Deterministic regex polish on issue-facing prose. Annotations only (never block); each finding carries a path so the agent can fix and re-run.
_polish_paths_comment: Prose fields the polish_grammar check scans.

deterministic_checks.description: Layer-1 jsonschema (draft-07) validation of the whole artifact against the manifest output_schema, before any other check. Annotate during a trial window; promote to block once outputs are confirmed to conform.

Detection only. Flags every high-weight claim stating a figure/date/vote so the triage judge must verify it against the cited extracts. Never blocks (route diagnostic); a wrong figure blocks only via the judge verdict.
claim_type -> allowed source_types (source_hierarchy). A high-weight claim citing a disallowed source type blocks; others annotate. A claim_type with no entry yields a non-blocking diagnostic.
organization_slug, list, and generated_for_run_id must be present and non-empty at the artifact root.
Every high-weight or blockable claim must carry at least one non-empty source_extract.
Every claim must carry at least one source_id AND at least one non-empty source_extract. Blocks if any failing claim is high-weight/blockable; annotates otherwise.
Every source_id referenced by a claim must resolve to a source in the top-level sources[].
Every source must carry non-empty retrieved_text_or_snapshot content.

Every source_extract must appear (exact substring or fuzzy >= substring_check.fuzzy_threshold) in the retrieved_text_or_snapshot of one of the claim's cited sources. High-weight failures block; others annotate. This enforces the rubric's 'the source body actually states the attributed claim' step and catches snippet-misreads and fabricated extracts.
Issue prose must meet the low substance floors in spec.completeness. Annotate only; a tight 1-to-3-issue list is correct.
Regex polish on issue-facing prose (spec.polish_paths). Never blocks; each finding carries a path to locate and fix.

HEAD probe (GET retry on 403/405) of every sources[].url. SSRF-hardened. Non-200/unreachable/rejected URLs annotate (warn), never block — matching the rubric, which keeps a dead cited link as Unverified rather than a hard fail when the fact is corroborated elsewhere.
